title: How Much Does It Cost to Rent a Villa in Phuket in 2026?
excerpt: Real long-term rental prices from 326 properties on our books, broken down by area and by bedroom count — plus the costs that never appear in the advertised rent.
author: Islander Home Team
content:
Most "Phuket rental price" articles quote a single number for the whole island, which is useless — a three-bedroom house in Kathu and a three-bedroom villa in Bang Tao are not the same product, and they are not within a factor of three of each other in price.

So here are the actual figures from our own long-term rental book: 326 properties currently advertised for monthly rental across ten areas of Phuket. These are asking prices as listed, not survey estimates.

Long-term rental prices by area

The "typical range" column drops the cheapest and most expensive tenth of each area, because every area has one outlier that distorts the picture. The median is the honest middle.

AreaListingsTypical range / monthMedian
Bang Tao59฿27,000 – ฿280,000฿100,000
Chalong58฿40,000 – ฿200,000฿85,000
Rawai48฿35,000 – ฿250,000฿90,000
Koh Kaew45฿37,000 – ฿80,000฿55,000
Kathu40฿15,000 – ฿80,000฿30,000
Thalang35฿29,000 – ฿180,000฿50,000
Phuket Town28฿18,000 – ฿45,000฿23,000
Patong7฿20,000 – ฿150,000฿40,000
Kamala5฿28,000 – ฿280,000฿35,000

Two things jump out of that table.

Phuket Town and Kathu are half the price of everywhere else. A ฿23,000 median in Phuket Town against ฿100,000 in Bang Tao is not a small gradient — it is a different budget entirely. If you work in town, or your children go to school on the east side, you are paying a very large premium to live on the west coast beaches.

Koh Kaew is the most predictable area on the island. Its typical range is only ฿37,000–฿80,000, the tightest of any area we cover. That is because the stock is dominated by modern estate villas and condominiums built to similar specifications, rather than a mix of ฿20,000 townhouses and ฿600,000 beachfront estates.

Prices by bedroom count

If you are budgeting before you have chosen an area, this is the more useful cut:

SizeListingsTypical range / monthMedian
1 bedroom62฿15,000 – ฿35,000฿23,000
2 bedrooms59฿29,000 – ฿100,000฿50,000
3 bedrooms119฿35,000 – ฿180,000฿55,000
4 bedrooms60฿55,000 – ฿300,000฿90,000

Note how wide the three- and four-bedroom bands are. At that size, location and whether there is a private pool matter more than the bedroom count itself. A three-bedroom townhouse in Kathu and a three-bedroom pool villa in Layan are both "3 bed", and there is a ฿150,000 gap between them.

What the advertised rent does not include

This is where budgets go wrong. On a typical Phuket long-term rental:

  • Electricity is not included, and it is the big one. Air conditioning in a pool villa through the hot season regularly runs ฿8,000–฿20,000 a month. Ask what the last tenant actually paid before you sign.
  • Water and internet are usually not included, though both are minor — a few hundred to about ฿1,000 each.
  • Common area maintenance in an estate or condominium is often included in the advertised rent, but confirm it. Where it is not, expect roughly ฿50 per square metre per month.
  • Pool and garden service is normally the landlord's cost on a villa. Get it in the contract; it is the most commonly disputed item.
  • A two-month security deposit plus the first month up front is the standard structure. Twelve-month contracts are the norm; six months is possible at a premium of roughly 10–20%.

Where the rent actually moves

Two levers move the number more than anything else, and both are in your control:

Contract length. The prices above are yearly rates. The same villa on a three- or six-month contract typically lists 20–40% higher per month, and on a nightly holiday basis it can be several times the long-term rate. If you can commit to twelve months, say so in the first message — it is the single strongest thing you can bring to a negotiation.

Season. Phuket's high season runs roughly November to April. Owners are far more flexible on a long-term rate in May–September, when the alternative is an empty house.

Start with the area, not the price

Our advice, after matching a lot of tenants: pick the area first, on your commute and your daily life, then set the budget. People who do it the other way round tend to end up in a beautiful villa forty-five minutes from everything they actually do.

Every area page below shows what is genuinely available right now, with current asking prices:

  • Bang Tao rentals — Laguna, Cherng Talay and Layan; the island's luxury lifestyle strip
  • Rawai rentals — the quieter, more residential south, popular with long-stay families
  • Chalong rentals — central and well connected, with a wide spread of villa stock
  • Koh Kaew rentals — near the international schools and Central Floresta
  • Kathu rentals — the best value on the island, ten minutes from Patong
  • Thalang rentals — space and land for the money, in the north
  • Phuket Town rentals — town living, the cheapest bracket we cover

If you would rather just tell us the budget and the school run and let us shortlist, send us the requirements — that is the part we are actually good at.
